extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and patent examiners operating before the CNIPA (China)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and examination criteria from the CNIPA's revised Guidelines for Patent Examination (effective Jan 1, 2026), covering statutory patentability limits, procedural requirements, AI/bitstream guidance, disclosure requirements, fees, and invalidation/priority rules for Chinese patent practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor identity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor shall be an individual (i.e., a natural person). The request form shall include the identity information of all inventors, ensuring the information is true. False inventors must not be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request form shall not include an entity or collective, or the name of the artificial intelligence, such as '×× Research Group' or 'Artificial Intelligence ××'. In the examination process, examiners generally do not examine whether the inventor listed meets the requirement unless evidence suggests otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of applicant and agency identity/contact info
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent agencies shall verify the applicant’s identity information and contact information filled in the request form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent agency or patent attorney applies for a patent or requests invalidation in its own name, it shall be handled in accordance with the Patent Agency Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application priority declaration rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original application of a divisional application claims priority, but the applicant did not declare that priority was claimed in the request when filing the divisional application, the divisional application shall be deemed not to have claimed priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner shall issue a notice of deemed non-claim of priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animals and plant varieties excluded from patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Article 25, Paragraph 1, Item (4) of the Patent Law, animal and plant varieties cannot be granted patent rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provided: 'animal' excludes humans and refers to organisms that cannot synthesize their own nutrients; 'plant variety' refers to a group of plants artificially selected or discovered and improved with consistent morphological/biological characteristics and relatively stable genetic traits. New plant varieties may be protected under other laws (e.g., Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous utility model and invention application handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If the same applicant applies for both a utility model patent and an invention patent for the same invention on the same day, the applicant should state in each application that another patent has already been applied for for the same invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no statement is made, Article 9(1) applies (only one patent right can be granted). If a statement is made and the invention patent passes examination, the applicant should be notified to declare abandonment of the utility model within a prescribed period; if they do, grant the invention patent and announce the abandonment. If the applicant disagrees, the invention application is rejected; failure to respond results in deemed withdrawal. If abandoning a granted utility model, a written statement of abandonment must be attached when responding to examination opinion; notice of grant issued and statement registered/published noting termination date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step evaluation on claimed technical solution as a whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an invention possesses inventiveness is determined in relation to the claimed invention; the evaluation should be conducted on the technical solution defined by the claims, i.e., the entire technical solution, rather than a single technical feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical features that contribute to prior art or produce unexpected technical effects should be included in the claims; otherwise, even if described in the specification, they will not be considered in evaluating inventiveness. Features that do not contribute to solving the technical problem generally will not affect inventiveness even if included in the claims. Example: adding conventional/irrelevant features (housing shape, screen size) that do not contribute to the technical solution won't confer inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination principle for algorithmic features and business rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For invention patent applications that contain algorithmic features or business rules and methods, the examination should be conducted on the claimed solution as a whole: consider technical means involved, the technical problem solved, and the technical effects achieved; technical features should not be simply separated from algorithmic or business/methodological features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All contents recorded in the claims should be taken together in the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest / legality / social morality bar for algorithmic applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention patent applications containing algorithmic features or business rules and methods cannot be granted patent rights if they contain content that violates the law, social morality, or harms the public interest (Article 5, Paragraph 1 of the Patent Law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) A big-data in-store mattress sales system using facial recognition and identity information collected without lawful necessity was held to violate personal information protection rules and thus cannot be granted; (2) An autonomous vehicle emergency decision-making model that discriminates based on pedestrian gender and age violates social morality and cannot be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between non-patentable rules/methods and technical solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithmic features or business rules/methods that fall within rules and methods for intellectual activities (Article 25(1)(ii)) are not subject to patent protection. Conversely, algorithmic/business-rule-containing solutions that utilize technical means to solve technical problems and obtain technical effects fall under the technical solutions in Article 2(2) and are patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance clarifies when algorithmic/content is merely intellectual activity versus when it is integrated with technical means producing technical effects (thus patentable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of contribution of algorithmic features to inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: When conducting an inventive step examination, the contribution of algorithmic features or business rules and methods that are functionally mutually supportive and interactive with the technical features to the technical solution should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (e.g., scrap steel grading) show algorithmic adjustments (layer/level settings) that materially improve technical accuracy should be credited in inventive-step analysis if not disclosed by prior art or common knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification disclosure requirements for AI models and algorithmic inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification of an invention patent application that includes algorithmic features or business rules and methodological features should clearly and completely describe the solution adopted to solve its technical problem, including necessary modules, levels, or connections of the model and the specific steps and parameters required for training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the invention involves application of an AI model in a specific field/scenario, describe how the model/algorithm is combined with the field/scenario, and how input/output data are set to indicate inherent relationships so that a person skilled in the art can implement the solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure (Article 26(3))—what is required
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications must disclose enough detail (e.g., key indicators, causal relationships, validation data) for a person skilled in the art to determine that the solution can solve the technical problem claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A cancer-prediction application failing to specify which blood/biochemistry indicators are key, their weights, causal links to prediction, or validation data was held non-compliant with Article 26(3). Lack of proof that the solution improves accuracy means insufficient disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: When common knowledge/model architecture suffices for disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where model architectures or known algorithms are used, a clearly described hierarchical structure and input/output relationships can be sufficient for full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A facial-feature generation method using standard CNNs and a spatial transformation network was found to be fully disclosed because those skilled in the art can construct corresponding architectures from the description and known algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bitstream subject-matter exclusion (simple bitstreams not patentable)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the subject matter of a claim relates only to a simple bitstream, then the claim falls under rules and methods for intellectual activities (Article 25(1)(ii)) and is not subject to patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: claims that merely define a bitstream by listing syntax elements (e.g., 'A bitstream, characterized in that it includes syntax element A, syntax element B…') or that are titled as a 'method for generating a bitstream' but only define the bitstream content are non-patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bitstream-related technical solutions can be patentable when tied to specific coding methods
rubrics_metrics.description: If a specific video encoding method for generating a bitstream falls under the technical solution of Article 2(2), then the method for storing/transmitting the bitstream and the computer-readable storage medium for storing the bitstream (as defined by that specific method) can be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Storage or transmission methods and storage media should achieve optimized allocation of storage/transmission resources and be based on the specific video coding method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification drafting requirements for bitstream inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification of an invention patent application containing a bitstream generated by a specific video coding method should clearly and completely describe that specific video coding method so that a person skilled in the art can implement it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subject relates to storing/transmitting the bitstream or a computer-readable medium, the specification should include corresponding description to support those claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting guidance for bitstream/storage/transmission/media claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications that include bitstreams generated by a specific video coding method can be drafted as claims for storage methods, transmission methods, and computer-readable storage media, and such claims should generally be based on claims related to the specific video coding method or include all features of those methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example claim set shows method/device/media claims anchored to a video encoding method claim, with subsequent storage/transmission/media claims referencing the method or including its features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority evidence requirements for international-phase priority
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where a valid declaration of priority was not made during the international phase, the applicant shall submit relevant supporting documents. These supporting documents shall be signed or sealed by all applicants of the prior application. The supporting documents shall be originals or notarized copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to ensure priority is supported when not declared at the international phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-acceptance of repeat invalidation requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for invalidation is filed again for a patent right already examined based on the same or substantially the same reasons and evidence, it will not be accepted or examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exception is where reasons or evidence were not considered by the prior decision due to time limits or other reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation request sincerity (true intention) ground
rubrics_metrics.description: A new ground for non-acceptance: the request for invalidation was not made in accordance with the true intention of the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is added as a separate basis for refusal to accept an invalidation request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting amended/modified texts in invalidation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patentee amends the claims, he/she shall submit the full replacement pages and a comparison table of the amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple amended texts submitted by the patentee in the same invalidation hearing proceedings all comply, the last amended text shall prevail; remaining amended texts shall not be used as the basis for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application surcharge threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: An application surcharge is payable when the description (including drawings and sequence lists) of the application documents exceeds 30 pages or the claims exceed 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amount of the fee is calculated based on the number of pages or claims. For computer-readable sequence lists submitted in the prescribed format, the page count is not included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances allowing refunds of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated refund circumstances: overpayment; duplicate fee payment (e.g., paying the same bibliographic change fee twice); incorrect payment (wrong fee type or application number); deemed-withdrawn/deemed-not-filed before substantive-stage notification; voluntary withdrawal before first-exam-response deadline (refund 50% of substantive exam fee if no response submitted); refund of annual fee after termination/invalidity announcement; refund of request-to-restore-rights fee if Patent Office decides not to restore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific amounts and examples provided (e.g., overpayment refund of difference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination modes: priority, expedited, deferred, rapid examination
rubrics_metrics.description: At the applicant’s request, patent applications may be examined as needed, including priority examination, expedited examination, or deferred examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid Examination (new): applications that passed preliminary examination by a national-level intellectual property protection center or rapid rights protection center and meet relevant regulations can be examined quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term adjustment publication content
rubrics_metrics.description: Items published for patent term adjustment include: main classification number, patent number, application date, authorization announcement date, original patent term expiration date, and current patent term expiration date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pharmaceutical product patent term extensions, publication items include drug name and approved indications in addition to the above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent licensing agreement publication items
rubrics_metrics.description: The items included in the filing and publication of a patent licensing agreement include: main classification number, patent number, filing number, licensor, licensee, invention name, application date, invention publication date, authorization announcement date, license type (exclusive, exclusive, ordinary), and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items for announcement of changes and cancellation of filings are similarly specified (e.g., change content, dates, termination date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor/applicant name recorded for international/divisional filings
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications or divisional applications, the name of the inventor or designer, or the name of the applicant, recorded on the patent certificate at the patent application date refers to the name at the time the international application entered the Chinese national phase or the date the divisional application was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies which point in time governs the name recorded on the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable delays in authorization process
rubrics_metrics.description: The following delays are considered reasonable delays in the authorization process: re-examination procedures for amending patent application documents (Article 66 of the Implementing Regulations); suspension procedures (Article 103); preservation measures (Article 104); re-examination procedures for revoking a rejection decision based on new reasons or evidence submitted by the re-examination requester; and administrative litigation procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are recognized as justifying extensions/delays in the authorization timetable.
